get.description:
Returns every managed database record in the cluster, with live/down
status merged in from node heartbeats (Pro feature). Secrets are
redacted; use the connection endpoint to read them.
get.summary: List all managed databases

post.description:
Creates a single-node postgres container on THIS node and records
it in the cluster store (Pro feature). Not scheduled: the node that
serves this request becomes the instance's home node.

Restores one snapshot of an instance's backup into a BRAND-NEW
instance on the node serving this request (Pro feature). The source
instance is never modified. Each logical database in the snapshot is
recreated with a FRESHLY generated role password — the roles in the
backup's globals.sql carry password hashes the cluster cannot
reproduce, so that file is kept for manual recovery only.
The repository must be reachable from this node.
Partial failures are reported per database in the response body; the
new instance is kept either way.
post.summary: Restore a managed database backup into a new instance

get.description:
Returns one record with live status and, when the home node answers,
its container/server state (Pro feature). Secrets are redacted.
get.summary: Get a managed database

put.description:
Changes settings that do not require recreating the container —
currently only the constellation restriction, which is re-applied to
the instance's proxy route on its home node (Pro feature).

delete.description:
Stops and removes the instance's container on its home node and drops
the record (Pro feature). The data volume is KEPT unless
?removeVolume=true is passed.

put.description:
Sets the restic repository and schedules for an instance's backups
(Pro feature). The repository is interpreted on the instance's HOME
node and is initialised lazily, on the first run. The repository
password is generated once and never rotated by this endpoint, since
it is the only key to the existing snapshots.
put.summary: Configure backups for a managed database

delete.description:
Clears the instance's backup settings and deregisters its scheduled
jobs (Pro feature). The restic repository and every snapshot in it
are left untouched — but the password is dropped with the record, so
recovering those snapshots afterwards means recovering the password
from the backup password log.
delete.summary: Remove a managed database's backup configuration

post.description:
Starts a backup of the instance on its home node and returns
immediately (Pro feature): a dump plus an upload is unbounded work.
Progress and outcome are reported through the instance's events and
through the snapshot listing.
post.summary: Back up a managed database now

get.description:
Returns the restic snapshots tagged for this instance, newest first
(Pro feature). An empty list is returned — not an error — while the
repository has not been written to yet.
get.summary: List a managed database's backup snapshots

get.description:
Returns the superuser credentials and connection URL for an instance,
plus one URL per logical database (Pro feature). This is the only
endpoint that returns secrets.
get.summary: Get connection info for a managed database

post.description:
Creates one application database inside an instance, owned by a
freshly generated role scoped to it (Pro feature). Returns the
credentials once, in the response.
post.summary: Create a logical database and role

delete.description:
Drops one application database inside an instance, terminating its
open sessions first (Pro feature). Destroys that database's data.
delete.summary: Delete a logical database and its role

post.description:
Generates a new password for one application role and returns the new
connection URL (Pro feature). Existing sessions keep working until
they reconnect.
post.summary: Rotate a logical database role's password

get.summary: List package registries

post.description:
Claims the name, provisions the backing bucket and marks the registry ready.
Every type but static is served on the given host from then on; a static
registry publishes its sites instead (Pro feature).

get.description: Returns the registry with the nodes serving it and its stored-size rollup, secrets redacted (Pro feature)
get.summary: Get one package registry

delete.description:
Removes the record and every metadata key; serving nodes withdraw
the endpoint. Stored blobs are PRESERVED unless purgeData=true,
which best-effort empties the backing bucket (the bucket itself is
left in place) (Pro feature).

post.description:
Starts a mark-and-sweep of the registry's blob store and reconciles its
stored-size and package counters. Returns 202 immediately; the outcome
arrives as a cosmos.registry.gc event. Blobs younger than 24 hours are
never collected, whether or not anything references them (Pro feature).
post.summary: Run a registry's garbage collection now

get.description:
Returns every package with its versions and their files. Works for every
registry type but static: a docker image's versions are its manifests
(named by digest, with the tags resolving to each), an npm package's are
its published versions with their dist-tags (Pro feature)
get.summary: List the packages of a registry

get.description: Returns the package with its versions and files (Pro feature)
get.summary: Get one package

delete.description:
Removes the package and every version; the stored files are reclaimed by the next GC pass.
Accepts a Cosmos token or a registry deploy token with push scope (Pro feature).

post.description:
Stores one or more files under a version. Accepts a multipart form (every
file part is stored under its own filename) or a single raw file as the
request body, in which case the filename query parameter is required.
Query parameters: version (default: a UTC timestamp), filename. A file
that already exists in the version is refused (409): upload a new version
or delete it first. Accepts a Cosmos token with the Resources permission
OR a registry deploy token with push scope on an access that exposes this
registry (Pro feature).
post.summary: Upload files into a generic package version

parameters.description: Filename, required for a raw body
parameters.name: filename

delete.description:
Removes the version and its file entries; the stored files are reclaimed
by the next GC pass. For generic and pypi, "latest" is re-pointed at the
newest remaining version; for docker (a manifest, by digest) and npm every
tag resolving to the deleted version is dropped instead (Pro feature).

get.description:
Streams the file (the version may be "latest"); accepts a Cosmos token
with the Resources read permission OR a registry deploy token with pull
scope (Pro feature).
get.summary: Download one file of a package version

delete.description:
Removes the file entry, and the version when it was its last file; the stored bytes are
reclaimed by the next GC pass. Refused for docker and npm, whose versions are deleted whole.
Accepts a Cosmos token or a registry deploy token with push scope (Pro feature).
delete.summary: Delete one file of a package version

put.description:
Replaces the quota, the host, the visibility, the anonymous-pull policy, the
serving tags or the whole user-facing route. Absent fields keep their stored
value (Pro feature).

get.description:
Returns every site with its deployments, which one is active, and its
route configuration (Pro feature)
get.summary: List the sites of a static registry

get.description: Returns the site with its deployments (Pro feature)
get.summary: Get one static site

put.description:
Replaces the site's route configuration (host, internal, spa, tags or the whole user-facing
route); absent fields keep their stored value. Admin only: a deploy token cannot move a site (Pro feature).

delete.description: Removes the site and all its deployments; the stored zips are reclaimed by the next GC pass (Pro feature)

post.description:
Moves the site's active pointer. This is BOTH deploy and rollback: the
deployments are immutable, so switching between them is instant and
cannot half-apply. Accepts a Cosmos token with the Resources permission
OR a registry deploy token with push scope (Pro feature).

Stores a zip as one immutable deployment. Accepts a multipart form
(field "file") or the raw zip as the request body. Query parameters:
version (default: a UTC timestamp), activate (default true for the
site's first deployment), host/internal/spa/tags to configure the
site's route on first upload. Accepts a Cosmos token with the
Resources permission OR a deploy token of this registry with push scope
(Pro feature).

delete.description:
Removes the deployment record; the stored zip is reclaimed by the next
GC pass. Refused for the deployment that is currently active (Pro feature).

get.description:
Streams the zip exactly as it was uploaded (the version may be "active"
for the one currently served). Accepts a Cosmos token with the Resources
read permission OR a registry deploy token with pull scope (Pro feature).
get.summary: Download one static-site deployment archive

post.description:
Creates a deploy token on the registry. The raw token is returned ONCE, in this
response, and never stored. Scopes default to pull+push (Pro feature).

delete.description:
Removes the token; it stops working on this node at once and on the others
within their cache TTL (Pro feature).

a fill-mode volume-server deployment on the chosen tags, a filer+S3
deployment behind the tunnel LB, and a managed postgres for the filer

put.description:
Replaces the user-facing settings of the instance's S3 route (auth,
shield, whitelist...). Name, mode, target, tunnel and owner are
forced server-side; the restriction flag is mirrored onto the record.
The route lives in the filer deployment's compose, so this is a compose
rewrite + version bump; nodes apply it without recreating the filers
(Pro feature).
put.summary: Update the S3 endpoint's proxy route

get.description:
Returns the unredacted instance status (S3 access and secret keys included) and

get.summary: Get a managed SeaweedFS instance with its S3 credentials

put.description:
Sets the storage cap per node (0 = unlimited) and rolls the volume servers one node at a
time. Lowering it below what a node holds deletes nothing: the node just stops receiving
new volumes until it is back under the cap (Pro feature).
put.summary: Change the per-node storage cap of a managed SeaweedFS instance

post.description:
Starts a rolling upgrade to the given image: the masters one at a time, then the volume
and filer deployments one node at a time (Pro feature).

get.description:

post.description:
Body is a state file as produced by the export. Writes every record that does not already

Removes the import-in-progress marker left by a failed import or reseed, accepting the
deployments bucket as it is and letting the scheduler reconcile again. Pro feature.

put.description: Creates the explicit zone, or replaces it. A zone is a domain with its HTTPS setup (certificate mode, DNS challenge provider, wildcard) and its DynDNS setup. Every hostname under the domain uses it, unless a longer zone matches. The certificate mode is LETSENCRYPT, SELFSIGNED, PROVIDED (TLSCert and TLSKey in PEM format) or DISABLED (plain HTTP), and no server-wide mode overrides it. Replicated to the whole Constellation. Credentials sent empty by a client without the credentials permission keep their current value, and so does the private key of a provided certificate, which is never returned.

httpscertificateMode.description:
HTTPS setup. The mode is LETSENCRYPT, SELFSIGNED, PROVIDED (the
certificate below) or DISABLED (the hostnames are served over plain HTTP).
The zone decides alone: no server has an HTTPS mode of its own to
override it, only the choice of not serving HTTPS at all.

issuesCertificate.description:
IssuesCertificate is true when the zone gets a certificate of its own
through its DNS provider; its hostnames use this node's one otherwise

records.description:
Records is the DynDNS state of the zone, only known by the node writing
the records (this node when standalone, the cluster leader otherwise)

recordsSupported.description: RecordsSupported is true when the DNS provider of the zone can manage records

deviceName.description: Empty means "this node" (full edit); set means a remote tags-only edit.

argsEscaped.description: True if command is already escaped (meaning treat as a command line) (Windows specific).

attachStdin.description: Attach the standard input, makes possible user interaction

cmd.description: Command to run when starting the container

entrypoint.description: Entrypoint to run when starting the container

env.description: List of environment variable to set in the container

healthcheck.description: Healthcheck describes how to check the container is healthy

image.description: Name of the image as it was passed by the operator (e.g. could be symbolic)

labels.description: List of labels set to this container

macAddress.description:
Mac Address of the container.

Deprecated: this field is deprecated since API v1.44. Use EndpointSettings.MacAddress instead.

onBuild.description: ONBUILD metadata that were defined on the image Dockerfile

shell.description: Shell for shell-form of RUN, CMD, ENTRYPOINT

stdinOnce.description: If true, close stdin after the 1 attached client disconnects.

stopTimeout.description: Timeout (in seconds) to stop a container

tty.description: Attach standard streams to a tty, including stdin if it is not closed.

user.description: User that will run the command(s) inside the container, also support user:group

volumes.description: List of volumes (mounts) used for the container

workingDir.description: Current directory (PWD) in the command will be launched

interval.description: Zero means to inherit. Durations are expressed as integer nanoseconds.

retries.description:
Retries is the number of consecutive failures needed to consider a container as unhealthy.
Zero means inherit.

startInterval.description: The interval to attempt healthchecks at during the start period

startPeriod.description: The start period for the container to initialize before the retries starts to count down.

test.description:
Test is the test to perform to check that the container is healthy.
An empty slice means to inherit the default.
The options are:
{} : inherit healthcheck
{"NONE"} : disable healthcheck
{"CMD", args...} : exec arguments directly
{"CMD-SHELL", command} : run command with system's default shell

timeout.description: Timeout is the time to wait before considering the check to have hung.

dns.description: DNS replaces the DNS servers of the container when sent, an empty list for the default of Docker

interactive.description: we make this a int so that we can ignore 0

lastTagTime.description: LastTagTime is the date and time at which the image was last tagged.

databaseNodeName.description: Optional: overrides the node column on metrics rows. Defaults to the hostname when empty, which is what a single-node install wants.

licence.description:
Optional: Pro licence key — stored on the lighthouse config and
validated via utils.ProcessLicence at the end of setup.

postgresHost.description: Optional: point this node at a shared Postgres instead of the local SQL store

constellationConfig.description: ConstellationConfig is the constellation file of this server, as created on the cluster

hostname.description: Hostname overrides the one derived from the cluster domain (<device>.<cluster domain>)

preview.description: Preview only returns the hostname the server would take, nothing is saved

readOnlyForceRecursive.description: ReadOnlyForceRecursive raises an error if the mount cannot be made recursively read-only.

readOnlyNonRecursive.description:
ReadOnlyNonRecursive makes the mount non-recursively read-only, but still leaves the mount recursive
(unless NonRecursive is set to true in conjunction).

source.description:
Source specifies the name of the mount. Depending on mount type, this
may be a volume name or a host path, or even ignored.
Source is not supported for tmpfs (must be an empty value)

mode.description: Mode of the tmpfs upon creation

sizeBytes.description:
Size sets the size of the tmpfs, in bytes.

This will be converted to an operating system specific value
depending on the host. For example, on linux, it will be converted to
use a 'k', 'm' or 'g' syntax. BSD, though not widely supported with
docker, uses a straight byte value.

Percentages are not supported.

HostIp.description: HostIP is the host IP Address

hostPort.description: HostPort is the host port number

platform.description: Platform is the image platform (default: the build node's).

branch.description: Branch defaults to the project's default branch.

sha.description: SHA pins the commit; empty builds the branch head.

from.description: From is the project to copy from.

runtimeEnv.description: RuntimeEnv copies the runtime environment of the deploy template (deploy.template.env).

secrets.description: Secrets copies the project secrets, values and PR availability included.

environments.description:
Environments: branch glob -> environment. A branch matching no entry is
built but not deployed.

name.description: Name is the default target (deployment or site) name.

previewHost.description:
PreviewHost is the hostname template of previews; {{pr}} and {{name}}
are substituted ("pr-{{pr}}.preview.example.com").

pullRequests.description:
PullRequests enables preview deployments, one per open PR, named
<name>pr<number>, removed when the PR closes or after PreviewTTL.

healthcheck.description: Healthcheck is a command run inside the container (["CMD", ...]).

spa.description: SPA / Internal apply to static sites.

project.description:
Project names an existing project whose stored git credentials are used when Source has
neither a connection nor a token.

deployment.description: Deployment / Site is the target name; empty = the rule's default name.

env.description:
Env sets or overrides environment variables of the deployed
application for this environment only: the service the UI template
creates, or the cosmos.json services that take the artifact. Values
may use the build variables and the project secrets (${NAME}).

host.description: Host is the route hostname the target gets when CI creates it.

apiUrl.description:
APIURL overrides the provider API base for self-hosted instances;
empty derives it from the repository URL.

host.description:
Host is the git host the token is valid for (github.com,
git.example.com). The UI offers the connection for repositories on
that host, and self-hosted repository listings derive the API base
from it; empty matches the provider's public host. A pasted URL is
reduced to its hostname on save.

provider.description: Provider is one of github, gitlab, gitea, bitbucket or git.

token.description:
Token authenticates clones and provider API calls. Write-only
through the API: reads answer "****" when set.

username.description:
Username pairs with Token for providers that need one (Bitbucket app
passwords, plain git basic auth). Defaults per provider.

lastBuildNumber.description: LastBuildNumber is the per-project build counter (CAS-bumped).

tags.description:
Tags select the nodes builds may run on (AND semantics, like
deployments). Empty = any node.

artifactQuotaBytes.description:
ArtifactQuotaBytes caps the project's stored file artifacts (0: the
default, ciDefaultArtifactQuota).

packageRegistry.description:
PackageRegistry receives the package of an npm / pypi strategy. Empty
on save picks the only registry of that type.

registry.description: Registry: the docker registry to push to (its host prefixes the image); Image: repository name (default: project name).

tokens.description: Tokens are Cosmos-minted deploy tokens keyed by registry. Never user-visible.

apiUrl.description:
APIURL overrides the provider API base for self-hosted GitLab / Gitea /
GitHub Enterprise; empty derives it from RepoURL.

branches.description:
Branches is the UI branch filter (globs). Empty = every branch. Rules
inside cosmos.json / .woodpecker.yml apply INSIDE this filter.

connection.description:
Connection names a CIGitConnection whose credentials this project
uses. When set, Token and Username below are ignored (and cleared on
save); APIURL still applies when given, else the connection's does.

defaultBranch.description: DefaultBranch is what a manual run builds when no branch is given.

repoUrl.description:
RepoURL is the https clone URL (https://github.com/owner/repo[.git]).
An ssh clone URL (git@host:owner/repo.git, ssh://host/owner/repo) is
accepted on save and converted to its https form: clones and provider
calls authenticate with the token over https.

rootDir.description: RootDir is the sub-folder to build (monorepos).

token.description:
Token authenticates clones and provider API calls (webhook creation,
commit statuses, collaborator checks) for a project without a
connection. Write-only through the API.

username.description:
Username pairs with Token for providers that need one (Bitbucket app
passwords, plain git basic auth). Defaults per provider.

providerHookId.description:
ProviderHookID is the id of the hook Cosmos created through the provider
API, when it could.

secret.description: Secret signs inbound deliveries (HMAC / shared token, per provider).

compose.description:
Compose is the service spec the nodes apply. Exclusive with Function:
a deployment declares one or the other (ValidateDeploymentSpec).

function.description:
Function makes this a function deployment: the compose is DERIVED from
it (one service per handler, see functions.go) when the scheduler
dispatches. Its Source.Token is redacted by the API and preserved across
user updates.

minReplicas.description:
MinReplicas/MaxReplicas switch the deployment to load-based autoscaling:
each reconcile cycle the leader targets the current replica count clamped
to [min,max], stepping up by one when the nodes running the deployment
average above DeployScaleUpThreshold busyness (max of CPU%/RAM% from
heartbeats) and down by one below DeployScaleDownThreshold, at most one
step per DeployScaleCooldown. Nodes without trusted metrics
(MonitoringOn=false) hold the count steady.
Use Tags to restrict which nodes autoscaled replicas may land on — the
same affinity filter as the other modes.

owner.description:
Owner marks a deployment as system-owned (e.g. "seaweedfs:<instance>").
Owned deployments are created and mutated exclusively by the owning Go
feature: the HTTP API refuses user create/update/delete on them so a UI
action can't desync the owner's record from the deployed spec. Empty for
every user-created deployment.

preserveVolumesOnRemove.description:
PreserveVolumesOnRemove keeps the deployment's named volumes on disk when a
replica is removed — a fill-mode scale-down (node untagged) or a full delete.
Stamped as the cosmos-deployment-keep-volumes label on the containers so the
node-side teardown honors it even for orphan removal, which runs after the
KV record is already gone. Used by system-owned data deployments (managed
SeaweedFS volume servers) where a stray untag must never destroy data.

replicaFill.description:
ReplicaFill switches the deployment to fill mode: exactly one replica on
EVERY alive, non-broken node matching Tags (every node when Tags is
empty — DaemonSet-style). The replica count follows the eligible node
set as nodes join/leave. Exclusive with the other two modes.

replicaFillMode.description:
ReplicaFillMode refines fill mode (only valid with ReplicaFill). The tag
set still defines the placement universe; the sub-mode sets how much of
it is occupied:
  - "full" (default, empty string): one replica on every eligible node,
    always.
  - "bare": load-based between 1 and the whole eligible set — the
    autoscale stepper (busyness thresholds + cooldown) with min=1 and
    max=eligible node count. Idle collapses to one replica.
  - "empty": bare, plus every container carries the cosmos-lazy label so
    the idle floor replica is stopped by the lazy layer and woken by the
    proxy on the next request — the tag scales from zero.

replicas.description:
Replicas is the fixed replica count (the original mode). Exactly one of
the three replica modes must be configured — fixed (Replicas), autoscale
(MinReplicas/MaxReplicas) or fill (ReplicaFill); ValidateReplicaConfig
enforces the exclusivity since struct tags can't express it. In every
mode, Tags restricts which nodes are eligible.

storage.description:
Storage lists RCLONE remote names this deployment depends on. Checked
node-side in executeApply before docker.CreateService runs — a missing
remote produces StatusFail and flows through the existing fail-streak
quarantine path. Not a placement filter: RCLONE config is cluster-synced
via constellation, so every eligible node has the same remote set.
${storage.NAME} in compose fields resolves to the mount path on apply.

strategy.description:
Strategy selects which PlacementStrategy the scheduler uses for this
deployment. Empty is treated as "round-robin" for back-compat with
KV entries written before this field existed.

tags.description:
Tags filter eligible placement nodes. A deployment with Tags=["gpu"]
will only land on nodes whose ConstellationDevice.Tags contains "gpu".
Multiple tags are AND'd: ["gpu","nvme"] requires both. Empty means no
filter — any node is eligible.

version.description:
Version is a monotonic integer bumped on every create/update. It is
server-assigned (the client never sets it) and is stamped onto every
container as the cosmos-deployment-version label so the scheduler can tell
a node running a stale spec from one running the current spec. A bump
triggers a rolling re-apply across the nodes already running the deployment;
see runReconcileCycle. Pre-version KV records and pre-version containers both
read as 0, so upgrading an existing install causes no spurious re-apply.

image.description:
Image overrides the runtime's default image (private mirror, patched
runtime); it must honour the same contract.

deployment.description:
Deployment is the deployment carrying the handler; on create, empty
means "fn<name>".

siblings.description: Siblings are the other handlers of the same deployment.

status.description: Status is "created" (no version pinned yet) or "deployed".

crontab.description: Crontab is the 6-field form used everywhere in Cosmos (seconds first).

version.description: Version to pin; empty or "latest" = the registry's latest.

entry.description:
Entry is FUNCTION_SOURCE: node = file inside the package, python =
module path. Empty = the package's main / import name.

env.description: Env is merged over the deployment-level env for this handler only.

route.description:
Route is the user-facing part of the function's URL (host, path, auth,
shield, restrictions...). Name, mode, target, tunnel and visibility are
forced when the compose is derived.

idleTTL.description:
IdleTTL is how long a replica stays awake without connections before the
lazy layer stops it (Go duration string).

package.description:
Package is the package name in that registry (npm name, possibly scoped;
PyPI project name, normalized on save).

registry.description:
Registry is the registry instance name; its type must match the runtime
(npm for node*, pypi for python*).

token.description:
Token is the read-only registry token minted for this function on the
registry (named "function-<name>"). Persisted, redacted in API output.

version.description:
Version is the PINNED version the deployment runs; set by deploy, never
a tag. Empty until the first deploy.

image.description: Image overrides the pinned default; never inferred from a running container.

port.description: Port overrides proxy listen-port allocation. Zero means "allocate one".

restrictToConstellation.description:
Pointer: the default is true, so a plain bool cannot tell "client sent
false" from "client omitted the field".

databases.description: Databases restricts what is restored; empty means every logical database.

newName.description: NewName is the instance to create. It must not exist.

port.description:
Port and RestrictToConstellation default as in a plain create (allocate a
port; restrict to the constellation).

snapshotId.description: SnapshotID is a restic snapshot id, long or short; "latest" works.

sourceName.description:
SourceName's backup configuration (repository AND password) is used to
read the snapshot; the source instance itself is never touched.

route.description: Route replaces the user-facing half of the proxy route; its RestrictToConstellation wins when both are sent.
Route's Host / RestrictToConstellation win over the scalars above when set.

type.description: Type is docker, npm, static, generic or pypi. Required and immutable afterwards.

route.description: Route's Host / RestrictToConstellation win over the scalars above when both are sent.
Route replaces the user-facing half of the serving route; its Host / RestrictToConstellation win over the scalars above.

bucket.description:
Bucket is the object-store bucket for both S3-family backends. Generated
as RegistryBucketName(name) for managed SeaweedFS.

path.description: Path is the filesystem root when Backend is "local".

seaweedfs.description: SeaweedFS is the managed instance name when Backend is "seaweedfs".

device.description: Device is the constellation device name of the volume server to evacuate.

newDevice.description: NewDevice is optional: the next live manager outside the master set is picked when absent.

restrictToConstellation.description:
*bool, deliberately: with a plain bool an EMPTY body would decode as
false and silently publish the object store — the exact inversion of the
restrict-by-default posture. Absent means invalid, never "unrestrict".

route.description: Route is required: the user-facing settings of the S3 route.

ecEnabled.description:
EC is OFF by default: encoding transiently needs a lot of disk headroom,
and ECMinFreeDiskPercent is a hard guard the job checks first.

repackCrontab.description:
Repack registers iff ECEnabled: EC shards never vacuum in place, so repack
is the only way deleted space inside an EC volume is reclaimed.

scrubEnabled.description: Scrub runs volume.check.disk to verify replica consistency (bitrot).

vacuumEnabled.description: Without vacuum, deleted data never frees disk and full volumes flip read-only.

Data.description:
Low-level storage metadata, provided as key/value pairs.

This information is driver-specific, and depends on the storage-driver
in use, and should be used for informational purposes only.

Required: true

Name.description:
Name of the storage driver.
Required: true

Id.description:
ID is the content-addressable ID of an image.

This identifier is a content-addressable digest calculated from the
image's configuration (which includes the digests of layers used by
the image).

Note that this digest differs from the `RepoDigests` below, which
holds digests of image manifests that reference the image.

VirtualSize.description:
VirtualSize is the total size of the image including all layers it is
composed of.

Deprecated: this field is omitted in API v1.44, but kept for backward compatibility. Use Size instead.

architecture.description: Architecture is the hardware CPU architecture that the image runs on.

author.description:
Author is the name of the author that was specified when committing the
image, or as specified through MAINTAINER (deprecated) in the Dockerfile.

comment.description:
Comment is an optional message that can be set when committing or
importing the image.

container.description:
Container is the ID of the container that was used to create the image.

Depending on how the image was created, this field may be empty.

Deprecated: this field is omitted in API v1.45, but kept for backward compatibility.

containerConfig.description:
ContainerConfig is an optional field containing the configuration of the
container that was last committed when creating the image.

Previous versions of Docker builder used this field to store build cache,
and it is not in active use anymore.

Deprecated: this field is omitted in API v1.45, but kept for backward compatibility.

created.description:
Created is the date and time at which the image was created, formatted in
RFC 3339 nano-seconds (time.RFC3339Nano).

This information is only available if present in the image,
and omitted otherwise.

dockerVersion.description:
DockerVersion is the version of Docker that was used to build the image.

Depending on how the image was created, this field may be empty.

graphDriver.description:
GraphDriver holds information about the storage driver used to store the
container's and image's filesystem.

metadata.description:
Metadata of the image in the local cache.

This information is local to the daemon, and not part of the image itself.

os.description: OS is the Operating System the image is built to run on.

osVersion.description:
OsVersion is the version of the Operating System the image is built to
run on (especially for Windows).

parent.description:
Parent is the ID of the parent image.

Depending on how the image was created, this field may be empty and
is only set for images that were built/created locally. This field
is empty if the image was pulled from an image registry.

repoDigests.description:
RepoDigests is a list of content-addressable digests of locally available
image manifests that the image is referenced from. Multiple manifests can
refer to the same image.

These digests are usually only available if the image was either pulled
from a registry, or if the image was pushed to a registry, which is when
the manifest is generated and its digest calculated.

repoTags.description:
RepoTags is a list of image names/tags in the local image cache that
reference this image.

Multiple image tags can refer to the same image, and this list may be
empty if no tags reference the image, in which case the image is
"untagged", in which case it can still be referenced by its ID.

rootFS.description:
RootFS contains information about the image's RootFS, including the
layer IDs.

size.description: Size is the total size of the image including all layers it is composed of.

variant.description: Variant is the CPU architecture variant (presently ARM-only).

ClusterDomain.description:
ClusterDomain is the domain servers joining with a constellation file get
their hostname under (<device>.<domain>). Empty: the zone of this server's hostname.

DoNotUseConstellationDNSOnHost.description:
DoNotUseConstellationDNSOnHost keeps the resolver of this server as it is.
Unset, the server uses the Constellation DNS on Pro and keeps its own
resolver on the community edition (see UseConstellationDNSOnHost).

httpscertificateMode.description:
HTTPS setup. The mode is LETSENCRYPT, SELFSIGNED, PROVIDED (the
certificate below) or DISABLED (the hostnames are served over plain HTTP).
The zone decides alone: no server has an HTTPS mode of its own to
override it, only the choice of not serving HTTPS at all.

nodeName.description: overrides the node column on metrics rows

AdvertisedAddress.description:
AdvertisedAddress is what the DNS records of this node point at: empty for
the detected public IP, "iface:<name>" for a network interface, or an IPv4

LocalCerts.description:
LocalCerts are the certificates this server gets by itself over HTTP-01,
one per domain, keyed by LocalCertZone. Never shared: each server
validates its own hostnames.

sslemail.description:
SSLEmail is the contact of the Let's Encrypt certificates. One for the
whole cluster, whichever server issues: SSLEmailShared is set once the
cluster's value was received, a server's own one from before is offered
to the cluster until then.

covered.description: Covered is false when the certificate served does not list the hostname

source.description:
Source is "zone", "node" (this node's own Let's Encrypt certificate),
"selfsigned", "provided" or "none" (HTTPS disabled)

ManagedByKind.description: ManagedByKind / ManagedByName identify the feature that owns this route (see ManagedByKinds); both empty for a user-created route.
